weakness.title: Missing Response to Physical Security Alerts
weakness.description: Physical security alerts are not followed by a response, because no one is assigned to act on them or the response comes too late to matter.

extended_description.applicability: Alerts of any origin that signal abnormal access or behavior, such as alarms, detectors, video analytics, access control events and observations by staff. A response includes verifying the alert, intervening and escalating. The speed required depends on the sensitivity of what is protected.
extended_description.exploitation: An unauthorized person continues to act after an alert has been raised, because nobody receives it, nobody is responsible for it, or the response arrives too late.

row.details: Alerts are raised but have no effect, so detection brings no protection.
Information, media and equipment can be viewed or removed while the alert is ignored.
Equipment can be altered or tampered with while the alert is ignored.

row.description: Name who receives each type of alert and who acts on it, with deputies for absences.
Write down what to verify, how to intervene and when to escalate, and set a response time for each level of sensitivity.

row.measure: Make sure alerts reach a person
row.description: Route alerts to a staffed station or a reachable on-call person, with a fallback when an alert is not acknowledged.
Provide responders with the access, communication and authority they need to act.
Run exercises and review real alerts, including false ones, to improve the response.
Responders must not be put at risk. Procedures must say when to call the police instead of intervening.

row.reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access
ISO/IEC 27001:2022, Annex A: 7.4 Physical security monitoring
